skill_tags: Sum to Infinity of a Geometric Progression

walkthrough:
Write expressions for the sums of the first 4 and first 8 terms:
$$p = S_4 = \frac{10(1 - r^4)}{1 - r}, \quad q = S_8 = \frac{10(1 - r^8)}{1 - r}$$

Set up and simplify the given ratio $\frac{p}{q} = \frac{16}{17}$:
$$\frac{p}{q} = \frac{10(1 - r^4)}{1 - r} \div \frac{10(1 - r^8)}{1 - r} = \frac{1 - r^4}{1 - r^8} = \frac{1 - r^4}{(1 - r^4)(1 + r^4)} = \frac{1}{1 + r^4} = \frac{16}{17}$$

Solve for the common ratio $r$:
$$1 + r^4 = \frac{17}{16} \implies r^4 = \frac{1}{16} \implies r^2 = \frac{1}{4} \implies r = \pm\frac{1}{2}$$

Calculate the sum to infinity $S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r}$ with $a = 10$ for each possible common ratio:
$$\text{For } r = \frac{1}{2}: \quad S_\infty = \frac{10}{1 - \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{10}{\frac{1}{2}} = 20$$
$$\text{For } r = -\frac{1}{2}: \quad S_\infty = \frac{10}{1 - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)} = \frac{10}{\frac{3}{2}} = \frac{20}{3}$$

ai_rubric.Sum to Infinity of a Geometric Progressi: Sets up ratio $\frac{1-r^4}{1-r^8} = \frac{16}{17}$ (M1, DM1). Solves for $r = \pm\frac{1}{2}$ (A1). Applies sum to infinity formula (DM1). Obtains both values $S_\infty = 20$ and $S_\infty = \frac{20}{3}$ (A1).
